strategy_objective_guidance:
- The evaluator scores only valid packings through

Execution must finish before the subprocess timeout, normally about 350 seconds.
- The reported sum is not scored and is not required to match the calculated sum; it only produces a warning when inconsistent. Nevertheless, report `np.sum(radii)` to avoid needless diagnostics. Runtime, symmetry, visual quality, method elegance, and proximity to the reference construction are not rewarded.
- Validity is near its maximum only when the construction is robustly feasible: one overlap or boundary violation collapses the entire score to zero. Once validity is secured, the largest remaining lever is the total radius sum. The target ratio can exceed 1; `2.635` is not a cap, so the highest-scoring program is simply the valid construction with the largest evaluator-computed sum, not necessarily one that merely reaches the reference.

This directly targets the scored sum and can refine unequal radii and boundary contacts.
- **Global stochastic search followed by feasibility polishing:** use `scipy.optimize.differential_evolution` over bounded center/radius variables with a penalty for boundary violations and pair overlaps, then pass the best candidate to `scipy.optimize.minimize` (`'SLSQP'` or `'trust-constr'`). strategies.title: [stripwise-radius-transfer] Two-row subsystem replacement

strategies.title: [triangular-defect-topology] Defected triangular-lattice exploration

strategies.plan:

strategies.title: [disk-cluster-swap] Discrete four-cluster exchange search
strategies.plan:

The falsifiable threshold is `2.63600`; success requires that the cluster exchange produce a sum above this value. strategies.plan:

The falsifiable threshold is a feasible sum above \(2.63700\). The new degree of freedom is a non-layered contact topology generated by sequential empty-space growth; the incumbent’s row parameterization cannot reach such a topology regardless of SLSQP tolerances.

Generate each row with boundary clearance based on the eventual LP radii: place the 7-circle row at `y=.085`, the 4-circle row at `y=.145`, and the remaining rows at approximately `.335`, `.555`, and `.775`, with alternating half-cell phases. For a 7-circle row use nominal spacing `1/7`; for a 4-circle row use spacing `1/4` and center it, rather than applying the incumbent’s fixed five-row spacing. This gives the LP a short, dense boundary layer and a wider compensating layer, allowing large circles to migrate into the four-circle defect. Reject seeds whose centers are outside `[0.03, .97]^2`, then run the existing feasibility tests unchanged.

The incumbent cannot create a four-circle compensating layer or a seven-circle boundary layer because every tested topology has only one six-circle row and four five-circle rows. The falsifiable acceptance threshold is a returned valid sum strictly above `2.63605`; below that threshold this topology enumeration is rejected as not beating the incumbent.

strategies.title: [boundary-shell-core-exchange] Explicit outer-shell plus interior-core replaceme
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: boundary-shell-core-exchange

Replacement scope: Replace the six adjacent-row subsystem solves with a fixed-topology shell/core optimization. Keep the incumbent row construction and global radius LP, but optimize four corner circles, eight wall-adjacent circles, and fourteen interior circles in three separate bounded nonlinear blocks.

Compute budget: Use exactly three block types, each solved once per candidate and revisited for two sweeps: corner block has 4 circles and at most 120 iterations, wall block has 8 circles and at most 100 iterations, and core block has 14 circles and at most 140 iterations. Use no more than four candidate allocations. The expected runtime is 10–25 seconds, comparable to the existing continuation stage.

Gain mechanism: The existing two-row blocks preserve row membership and therefore cannot exchange horizontal and vertical boundary clearance. Reclassify circles dynamically by current distance to the four walls, then optimize each block’s two coordinates and radius variables against all frozen circles. In the corner block, permit diagonal movement along the square corners; in the wall block, permit tangential sliding and independent radial growth; in the core block, permit non-row-preserving motion. After every block, solve the full radius LP and accept only candidates satisfying every boundary and pairwise constraint. This creates boundary-to-interior radius transfer without imposing row coordinates, while preserving a convex radius allocation for each fixed center set.

The new degree of freedom is tangential wall sliding plus block membership independent of rows, absent from the incumbent’s adjacent-row decomposition. The falsifiable acceptance threshold is a valid sum above `2.63610`; if no such candidate is produced, the exchange mechanism has not demonstrated a gain and should be discarded.

strategies.title: [variable-radius-triangular-seed] Multi-scale triangular-gap topology
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: variable-radius-triangular-seed

Replacement scope: Replace the entire row-seed construction and the continuation phase with a deterministic multiscale triangular-gap construction followed by one joint constrained solve. Retain the public interface, pair generation, LP sizing, and final independent validity check.

Compute budget: Use exactly six starts: three orientations of a 5-by-5 triangular lattice with one additional point in each of six selected interstitial gaps, and three starts obtained by reflecting those layouts. Run one SLSQP solve per start with at most 260 iterations and tight feasibility constraints; no other stochastic search is used. Expected evaluation time is 8–20 seconds.

Gain mechanism: Construct 25 points on a triangular lattice with horizontal spacing `h` and vertical spacing `sqrt(3)*h/2`, then insert one point into a large second-order triangular void while removing or displacing the nearest lattice point so that the total remains 26. Assign the inserted point an initial radius of `0.055` and the surrounding points `0.075`, then solve all 52 coordinates and 26 radii jointly. Use three defect locations: central, near the left-middle void, and near the lower-right void. The six layouts differ by reflection and by choosing the displaced point on the upper or lower side of the void. The joint constraints include all wall slacks and all 325 pair separations; after solving, recompute the radii by the fixed-center LP and shrink the final vector by `1e-8`.

This topology supplies a localized small-circle defect that can unlock otherwise unusable triangular void area and lets neighboring circles grow anisotropically; the incumbent’s row topology cannot realize this because every circle remains attached to one of five horizontal layers. The falsifiable acceptance threshold is a valid returned sum above `2.63620`; otherwise this higher-upside structural route is rejected.
